newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Cisco opens Israel development centre.
newsitem.headline: Cisco opens Israel development centre.

text.p: Cisco Systems Inc, the global leader in networking for the Internet, said on Wednesday it had opened an office in Israel to develop high-end gigabit switching and routing technology.

Officials of the U.S.-based company told a Tel Aviv news conference that its new office in the Mediterranean coastal town of Netanya hoped to meet an explosion in the Internet backbone bandwidth, which doubles every six to nine months.

"This is a development office of very high-tech high-speed routing and switching engines for our very high-end routing products," said James Richardson, president of Cisco Systems in Europe and the Middle East.
He said Israel, chosen because of the country's large concentration of talented engineers, was only the company's second development centre outside the United States. The other is in India.
The San Jose, California-based Cisco will start with 10 engineers in Israel and hopes to expand to 30 within a year. Officials declined to say how much of an investment they were making in Israel.

Richardson said more than 80 percent of the world's Internet traffic travels via Cisco Systems. The company anticipates revenues of $6 billion in fiscal year 1997 (August to July) compared with $4 billion in fiscal year 1996.
Joseph Gal, area manager for the Near East, told Reuters the company had decided to invest in Israel regardless of the Middle East political situation.
"Obviously if the political situation will be nice and easy, it will be easier for us to continue to invest," Gal said.
Other companies in the business, such as Intel, Microsoft and Motorola, also had had a good experience working in Israel and with Israeli talent, he added.
